prompt.content:
You expand an ISO 8601 repeating interval into the list of instants at which its occurrences start.

INPUT FORMAT
  R<count>/<start>/<duration>
  - <count> is a non-negative integer written in decimal digits. An unbounded "R" with no
    count is NOT accepted here.
  - <start> is an RFC 3339 date-time with a mandatory offset (e.g. 2026-01-31T00:00:00Z).
  - <duration> is an ISO 8601 duration.

DURATION GRAMMAR
  P[nY][nM][nW][nD][T[nH][nM][nS]]
  - Designators are UPPERCASE only.
  - Time components (H, M, S) may appear only after the "T". "P1S" is invalid; "PT1S" is valid.
  - "D" may not appear after the "T".
  - At least one component must be present. "P" and "PT" alone are invalid.
  - "W" may not be combined with any other component.
  - A decimal fraction is permitted ONLY on the seconds component, with at most 6 digits.

HOW TO EXPAND
  The first occurrence starts at <start>. Each later occurrence starts at the PREVIOUS
  occurrence plus the duration — the duration is applied iteratively, NOT multiplied and added
  to the original start. A count of 0 yields an empty list.

HOW TO ADD A DURATION TO AN INSTANT
  Apply the components in exactly this order:
    1. years
    2. months
    3. weeks and days
    4. hours, minutes, seconds
  After steps 1 and 2, if the resulting day-of-month does not exist in the resulting month,
  CLAMP it to the last day of that month. (31 January + 1 month = 28 February in a common
  year, 29 February in a leap year.) Leap years follow the proleptic Gregorian rule: divisible
  by 4, except centuries, except those divisible by 400.
  Steps 3 and 4 add exact elapsed time and never clamp.

OUTPUT
  Convert every occurrence to UTC and emit it as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS[.frac]Z, with trailing
  zeros removed from the fraction and the fraction dropped entirely when all its digits are
  zero.

  Reply with a single JSON object and nothing else, with exactly these three keys:
    {"valid": <true|false>, "occurrences": [<string>, ...] or null, "violation": <code or null>}
  When valid is true, violation MUST be null and occurrences MUST be the list (possibly empty).
  When valid is false, occurrences MUST be null.
  `valid` must be a JSON boolean, not a string.

VIOLATION CODES, IN PRECEDENCE ORDER
  Report the FIRST code that applies, in exactly this order:
    "shape"          -> not three "/"-separated parts, or the duration does not match the
                        grammar above (wrong case, D after T, time component without T, ...)
    "repeat-count"   -> the first part is not "R" followed by one or more decimal digits
    "timestamp"      -> the start is not a valid RFC 3339 date-time with an offset
    "duration-empty" -> the duration carries no components ("P", "PT")
    "week-mixed"     -> "W" is combined with another component
    "fraction"       -> a decimal fraction appears on a component other than seconds, or the
                        seconds fraction has more than 6 digits
